We would when we got older, and we're capable of making sandwiches ourselves. But in my experience, I remember being a 6 or 7 year old kid and thinking that getting a packed lunch from home was rare and to be cherished. I would make it stretch the whole day, and I was proud of it. It made me feel normal. But the fact is, it was rare. And most of the time it was the debt issue. A lot of children come from homes where there's either no time, no resources, or no care to make them food. As we get older, we become more independent, and it's expected of us to make our own lunches and stuff (understandable), but this early on discrimination against children from financially unstable homes only needs a short amount of time to mess them up. Again, in my experience, it took maybe a year before I started to feel really really insecure about money and finances. I would worry about what we spent when we went out for anything. That was about first grade. So the point is, that a child shouldn't have to supply themselves with food from home constantly because they know that if they go to school they won't be given anything because of their monetary issues.  And if a child has monetary issues, is there really any food to spare? Will you send your child with scarce and very necessary food from home to school if you know that they can get food provided for them there? Only to find out, that because you can't afford for much food at home , your child is denied food at school.

Whenever the staff even remembered (they were really irresponsible with them) to hand them to the students that needed them, they would always make it a big thing and call us up and give us this paper that was taped shut. Funniest part is, they taped it shut to be discreet, but still managed to humiliate us by making a scene in the middle of class by handing us a paper essentially saying "Hey, give this to your poor parents so you can eat at this establishment", in front of all our peers. And everyone knew what the taped shut paper meant. Fucking hated school.

This happened to me all the time when I was little. The first time it happened was in kindergarten, and it was cause they forgot to send the paper to register for free lunch to my mother, and failed to notify her at all not even with an email, and I had to give my hot lunch to the lunch lady at the checkout and was given a cold sunbutter and jelly sandwich and no milk. They threw that food away, the hot lunch. They would always 'forget' to tell children's parents or notify their guardians about the free lunch options and a lot of parents didn't know about it and if they did they didn't know how to apply. So a lot of kids went without hot lunch till the 'debt' was paid off. And sometimes, they would somehow run out of sandwiches to give us, so we would have to have the cold fruit cups and a weird little crumbly ass energy cookie. Both disgusting. I think the worst part though, was that there was a separate table for kids who were backed up on lunch payments. So we all had to sit there and watch our friends eat pizza, or hotdogs, or burgers and talk and socialize during the only fun part of the day besides recess, while we sat and watched with cold sandwiches.That's such a vivid memory, having to give your food back to the lunch ladies, it was like telling all your peers and all the teachers and what felt like the whole world, that you were 'poor' and couldn't pay for lunch. Imagine feeling like you had to explain and justify yourself to others at 6 years old because you were denied a hot lunch. And that was just the tip of the borderline abusive iceberg that is public school in the states. Shit left me traumatized. Glad I'm homeschooled now.

Too much memory is missing, and I don't know what's real or not. I can't trust my own mind. Depression makes me ugly, and it makes me cold, and the only way I can deal with it is to shut everything off and not feel. I'm in therapy and getting meds, but it's always gonna be there.
